chunks: Whereas earlier they had made a promise to God that they would never turn their backs; and a promise made to God is answerable.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'Wahadullah' in Surah Al-Azab?
ai.summary: This verse from Surah Al-Azab (33:15) references the covenant of the Banu Qurayza, who pledged not to flee during the Battle of the Confederate, yet broke their promise when the siege intensified. In Shia exegesis, this serves as a paradigm for the accountability of divine covenants ('Ahd Allah'), illustrating how a specific promise to God becomes a binding obligation subject to divine scrutiny. The verse underscores the gravity of breaking oaths made directly to Allah, linking historical betrayal with spiritual consequence.
